newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO plans U.S. listing for May 21.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO plans U.S. listing for May 21.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Monday that its planned flotation on the New York Stock Exchange would be in the form of American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) and would take place on Wednesday, May 21.
"We are planning the U.S. listing for May 21 and the prospectus will be published at the beginning of May," ABN AMRO chairman Jan Kalff told a news conference on the 1996 annual report.
In February ABN AMRO said it was planning a New York listing and that it would buy back one percent of its own shares for this purpose, which would be re-offered to U.S. investors.
Kalff said the secondary offering of the shares in the U.S. would have a value of some hundreds of million guilders.
Kalff said that ABN AMRO was busy forming a syndicate to manage the U.S. listing.
ABN AMRO reiterated it was still too early to give a forecast for 1997, and even if it could it would not do so before the U.S. listing went ahead on May 21.
He said that the bank was in the middle of a "quiet period" ahead of the listing.
"For this reason we are obliged not to give a specific statement (on ABN AMRO)," Kalff said.
